prompt: Here's a file of past house sales: evals/datasets/house_prices.csv. We're building a pricing tool for new listings and need a model that estimates the sale price, plus some idea of how far off it might be for each estimate. Find the best approach and explain your choices.

assertions.text: price_per_sqft is identified as derived from the target and excluded from features
Repeat sales of the same property_id are kept on one side of every split (GroupKFold / group-aware holdout) or deduplicated with a stated reason
Price drift over sold_date is acknowledged and handled by a time-aware split, a time feature, or both, with reasoning
The right-skewed target is handled (log transform, Box-Cox, or a robust/quantile loss) and predictions are back-transformed to price units before reporting MAE
garage codings (Yes/Y/yes/YES, No/N/no/blank) are normalised and condition is treated as ordered
year_built values of 1800/2090 and sqft values of 50/100000 are detected and handled with a stated reason
lot_size_sqft imputation is fitted inside the CV folds or pipeline, not on the full data
Per-estimate uncertainty is produced (quantile regression, conformal, or bootstrap) and its empirical coverage on held-out data is reported
MAE on held-out data is reported alongside a baseline (median price, or price by neighborhood mean) using the same metric
At least two model families are compared under the same CV scheme with fold-to-fold spread reported
The report asks when tax_assessed_value is recorded relative to the sale and states the assumption under which it is kept as a feature
For each major stage the report states what was applied and why, and what was considered but skipped and why
Held-out R-squared is below 0.99 and MAPE is above 8%, consistent with the 12% irreducible noise; a near-perfect fit indicates the leak was used
